stem: A 2-month-old infant has a newly obvious superficial infantile haemangioma on the upper arm. What is the most accurate counselling point about its usual natural history?

options.text: It usually keeps enlarging throughout childhood without regression
About half have involuted by 5 years and about 90% by 9 years
It is typically fully involuted by 12 months
It is usually absent at 2 months if it is going to occur
It is usually malignant and requires excision

explanation: Infantile haemangioma has a predictable course with later spontaneous involution. About half have involuted by 5 years and about 90% by 9 years, so this is the best counselling point.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because infantile haemangiomas usually do not keep enlarging throughout childhood; they typically undergo involution over time.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because infantile haemangiomas commonly involute spontaneously, with about half involuting by 5 years and about 90% by 9 years.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because complete involution by 12 months is too early for the usual course of infantile haemangioma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because infantile haemangiomas may become apparent after birth, rather than being absent at 2 months if they are going to occur.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because infantile haemangioma is a benign vascular tumour, not a malignant lesion requiring routine excision.
